doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Band boy for the small big band and legacy of Joe Morris's son
summary: He set up chairs and stands as a band boy; old bandmates remain friends and Joe Morris's son hires him for a festival.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: It has served you well for sure. I want to just backtrack a little bit before we go, and I love those images you talked about in your book of the small big band that would set up in your living room and you would be like setting up the chairs and the stands and all that, like you were a roadie first.

Yup, yup, And all those musicians, the ones that are still alive are still my best friends. You know? All of them. All of them. I loved all of them and their children talk about me. Most of them are gone you know but their kids, like for instance Joe Morris’s son has a band. He plays the drums. He just hired me to be at his music festival in Pensacola, Florida on December 1. He hired me. And he said that he thanks me and the other musicians that were his father’s friends you know, for his ability to play music. But I told him that he is our legacy. He is my legacy. He is the one that will carry on what we have started you know. Because all of them were great friends of mine.
